- When sentiment is negative (0.00 or -1.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (1.00) over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the first 3–5 days of a new 30-day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast to capture early momentum.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by shifting forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
